title: The Capxul rebuild
why: The product line drifted from its own description: facts were typed twice, and nothing proved the system did what it said.
what: Rebuild on one owner for every fact. The blueprint declares what Capxul does, the world says what runs where, and verdicts made by CI say what is proven. Every feature is measured by run records, not by code written.
endState: Capxul's own company runs a month on the rebuilt system in production, with every journey proven by CI and every measure watched.
outOfScope: New product features before the accounts pilot, and anything on main or integration/build, which carry the product work in flight.

title: Steps and logs are declared per operation, first drafted
what: Steps and logs are declared per operation, first drafted from the spans of measured runs. Every effectful function of our own code (Core, the world, the platform client, the runner's plumbing) is a span, Effect.fn with a name that is a declared step, imported from the blueprint and never written as a string; a lint rule fails a function of ours that does work without one, existing code by its ratchet. At run time a call fails when a step its operation declares is missing from the record while its path ran, or a refusal has no log naming the state or rule that refused. Library spans (postgres, HTTP GET and POST, rpc, bundler) are neither required nor forbidden, and the check ignores them. The waits a budget leaves out follow from the step kinds. Logs go through Effect's Logger, and the generic checks are written over OpenTelemetry spans and logs; the run-time checks of logs need 4.4
why: Milestone 4 needs it: Declared steps and logs, OpenTelemetry through the door, proof as verdicts, cost, the pipeline instrumented, one shared world with every journey side by side, the explainability eval, then the build evals
doneWhen: A passing run record, named in the roadmap's Proof column, is committed on master.

question: Share one world across every journey now, or after telemetry lands?
problem: Step 4.8 puts every journey side by side in one shared world, the biggest cut in the full run's time. It can start now, or wait until telemetry is on master.
context: A full run takes about thirty minutes against a target of five. When journeys share a world, a failure in one can show up in another, and without telemetry the record cannot say which call caused it.

rubric.name: Time to a faster run
rubric.why: Every day the run stays slow, every slice waits longer at its merge.

rubric.name: Explainable failures
rubric.why: A failure we cannot explain from its record costs a rerun, and reruns cost money under the daily cap.

options.title: Start now
options.detail: Build the shared world tonight on the runner's own records.
options.tradeoffs: The fastest cut, but a cross-journey failure is hard to explain until telemetry lands.

options.title: After telemetry
options.detail: Start once 4.4 is on master, with the isolation check reading spans.
options.tradeoffs: About a day later, but every failure names the call that caused it.

options.title: Company journeys first
options.detail: Share the world only for company journeys now; world journeys keep their own.
options.tradeoffs: Half the gain now with little risk; a second change later.

because: It takes most of the gain tonight while keeping the journeys whose failures are hardest to explain in worlds of their own.

question: Rename the glossary's old words in one sweep, or file by file on the ratchet?
problem: The glossary is declared and counts its old words: several thousand across the code. They can be renamed in one pull request or a file at a time.
context: Three lanes are building on master at once. A sweep touches most packages and would conflict with each of them; the ratchet lets each lane rename the files it already touches.

rubric.name: Conflicts with other lanes
rubric.why: A conflict stops a lane until someone merges by hand.

rubric.name: Time until the count is zero
rubric.why: Step 3.8 is done only when the old words are gone.

options.title: One sweep
options.detail: One builder renames every old word in one pull request tonight.
options.tradeoffs: Done in a day, but every open slice conflicts with it.

options.title: File by file
options.detail: Each lane renames the old words in the files it touches; the ratchet only falls.
options.tradeoffs: No conflicts, but the count falls slowly and 3.8 stays open for weeks.

because: Three lanes are mid-flight; a sweep would cost each of them a merge by hand for a step nothing else waits on.
